turns.user: Alan Turing là ai? Và hôm nay có tin gì mới về AI không?
turns.assistant_text:
## Alan Turing là ai?

Alan Mathison Turing (1912–1954) là nhà toán học, logic học và mật mã học người Anh. Ông được xem là một trong những nhà tiên phong của khoa học máy tính và trí tuệ nhân tạo.

- **Đóng góp lớn nhất trong AI:** phép thử Turing, đặt câu hỏi liệu máy móc có thể đạt được ý thức và suy nghĩ hay không.
- **Nền tảng khoa học máy tính:** ông hình thức hóa khái niệm thuật toán và tính toán bằng *máy Turing*, và góp phần phát triển luận đề Church-Turing.
- **Chiến tranh thế giới thứ hai:** ông làm việc tại Bletchley Park, trung tâm giải mã của Anh. Ông từng chỉ huy HUT 8, đơn vị giải mã hải quân Đức, và cải tiến máy bombe để tăng tốc phá mã.

Nguồn: [Wikipedia tiếng Việt – Alan Turing](https://vi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing)

## Tin AI mới hôm nay

Các bài dưới đây có ngày 10/11/2026 trong đường dẫn.

1. **Nvidia và scandal của Jensen Huang**
   - Axios cho biết cổ phiếu AI đã hồi phục, nhưng Nvidia vẫn yếu sau những tiết lộ cuối tuần từ CEO Jensen Huang. Thị trường cũng bị ảnh hưởng bởi kết quả bầu cử giữa kỳ Mỹ và nguy cơ đối với đà bùng nổ trung tâm dữ liệu. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley và JPMorgan đều cho rằng đợt giảm này có thể bị phản ứng quá mức.
   - [Axios: AI stocks bounce back — with one notable exception](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/10/ai-stocks-nvidia-broadcom)
   - The Conversation phân tích vì sao Nvidia thống trị thị trường AI, đồng thời nhắc đến vòng tài chính khép kín trong ngành và cuộc cạnh tranh chip Mỹ – Trung.
   - [The Conversation: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world…](https://theconversation.com/why-is-nvidia-so-powerful-in-the-ai-world-and-what-could-jensen-huangs-scandal-really-cost-296257)

2. **Lời khuyên y tế từ AI**
   - STAT lập luận rằng câu trả lời AI chính xác vẫn có thể gây hại, vì mỗi câu trả lời đều chọn lọc thông tin và ảnh hưởng đến hành vi. Bài viết đề xuất đánh giá "behavioral benchmarking" để đo tác hại dài hạn, không chỉ các rủi ro trước mắt. Theo bài, hơn 300 triệu người mỗi tuần hỏi ChatGPT về sức khỏe.
   - [STAT: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/ai-health-advice-accuracy-messaging-risk-behavioral-benchmarking)

3. **AI làm khó việc phát hiện cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả**
   - NPR đưa tin AI đang tạo ra các cuộc gọi swatting đáng tin để báo cảnh sát về vụ bắn súng hoặc tội phạm không có thật, khiến việc nhận diện ngày càng khó.
   - [NPR: AI is making it harder to detect fake emergency calls](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/nx-s1-5971477/ai-is-making-it-harder-to-detect-fake-emergency-calls)

4. **Quan điểm về AI và ngân hàng trực tuyến (bài bình luận)**
   - USA Today đăng bài opinion về việc ngân hàng đẩy mạnh giao dịch trực tuyến rồi đổ trách nhiệm khi bị tấn công, đồng thời bàn về việc con người ngày càng giao quyền kiểm soát đời sống hằng ngày cho máy móc. Đây là ý kiến cá nhân, không phải báo cáo sự kiện.
   - [USA Today: Banks push online banking, then blame us when we get hacked](https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/columnist/2026/11/10/ai-online-banking-vulnerable-hacking/92588938007)

Lưu ý: kết quả tìm kiếm chỉ cung cấp đoạn trích từ mỗi bài, nên chi tiết về cáo buộc liên quan đến Jensen Huang chưa được kiểm chứng. Nếu bạn cần chi tiết, mình có thể đọc toàn văn từng bài.

items.title: Alan Turing

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: A Holistic Assessment of the Carbon Footprint of Noor, a Very Large Arabic Language Model
items.summary: As ever larger language models grow more ubiquitous, it is crucial to consider their environmental impact. Characterised by extreme size and resource use, recent generations of models have been criticised for their voracious appetite for compute, and thus significant carbon footprint. Although reporting of carbon impact has grown more common in machine learning papers, this reporting is usually limited to compute resources used strictly for training. In this work, we propose a holistic assessment of the footprint of an extreme-scale language model, Noor. Noor is an ongoing project aiming to develop the largest multi-task Arabic language models -- with up to 13B parameters -- leveraging zero-shot generalisation to enable a wide range of downstream tasks via natural language instructions. We assess the total carbon bill of the entire project: starting with data collection and storage costs, including research and development budgets, pretraining costs, future serving estimates, and other exogenous costs necessary for this international cooperation. Notably, we find that inference costs and exogenous factors can have a significant impact on total budget. Finally, we discuss pathways to reduce the carbon footprint of extreme-scale models.

items.title: Enhancing Human-Like Responses in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper explores the advancements in making large language models (LLMs) more human-like. We focus on techniques that enhance natural language understanding, conversational coherence, and emotional intelligence in AI systems. The study evaluates various approaches, including fine-tuning with diverse datasets, incorporating psychological principles, and designing models that better mimic human reasoning patterns. Our findings demonstrate that these enhancements not only improve user interactions but also open new possibilities for AI applications across different domains. Future work will address the ethical implications and potential biases introduced by these human-like attributes.

items.title: Is Self-knowledge and Action Consistent or Not: Investigating Large Language Model's Personality
items.summary: In this study, we delve into the validity of conventional personality questionnaires in capturing the human-like personality traits of Large Language Models (LLMs). Our objective is to assess the congruence between the personality traits LLMs claim to possess and their demonstrated tendencies in real-world scenarios. By conducting an extensive examination of LLM outputs against observed human response patterns, we aim to understand the disjunction between self-knowledge and action in LLMs.

items.title: Large Language Models Lack Understanding of Character Composition of Words
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performances on a wide range of natural language tasks. Yet, LLMs' successes have been largely restricted to tasks concerning words, sentences, or documents, and it remains questionable how much they understand the minimal units of text, namely characters. In this paper, we examine contemporary LLMs regarding their ability to understand character composition of words, and show that most of them fail to reliably carry out even the simple tasks that can be handled by humans with perfection. We analyze their behaviors with comparison to token level performances, and discuss the potential directions for future research.

items.title: Unmasking the Shadows of AI: Investigating Deceptive Capabilities in Large Language Models
items.summary: This research critically navigates the intricate landscape of AI deception, concentrating on deceptive behaviours of Large Language Models (LLMs). My objective is to elucidate this issue, examine the discourse surrounding it, and subsequently delve into its categorization and ramifications. The essay initiates with an evaluation of the AI Safety Summit 2023 (ASS) and introduction of LLMs, emphasising multidimensional biases that underlie their deceptive behaviours.The literature review covers four types of deception categorised: Strategic deception, Imitation, Sycophancy, and Unfaithful Reasoning, along with the social implications and risks they entail. Lastly, I take an evaluative stance on various aspects related to navigating the persistent challenges of the deceptive AI. This encompasses considerations of international collaborative governance, the reconfigured engagement of individuals with AI, proposal of practical adjustments, and specific elements of digital education.
